warfarin.message: Foods high in vitamin K (leafy greens like spinach, kale) can reduce warfarin's blood-thinning effect. Consistent intake matters more than avoidance.

atorvastatin.message: Grapefruit juice can raise atorvastatin levels in the blood, increasing risk of muscle-related side effects.

simvastatin.message: Grapefruit juice can significantly raise simvastatin levels, increasing risk of serious muscle damage (rhabdomyolysis).

tranylcypromine.message: Tyramine-rich foods (aged cheese, cured/processed meats, some wines) can cause a dangerous spike in blood pressure with this medicine.

moclobemide.message: Tyramine-rich foods may interact with this medicine; risk is lower than with older MAOIs but caution is still advised.

doxycycline.message: Dairy products and calcium-rich foods can reduce absorption of doxycycline, making it less effective. Space apart by a couple of hours.

tetracycline.message: Dairy products and calcium-rich foods can significantly reduce absorption of tetracycline. Space apart by a couple of hours.

ciprofloxacin.message: Dairy products and calcium-rich foods can reduce absorption of ciprofloxacin. Space apart by a couple of hours.

metronidazole.message: Alcohol with metronidazole can cause a severe reaction (flushing, nausea, rapid heartbeat). Avoid alcohol during and for at least 24-48 hours after treatment.

disulfiram.message: This medicine is specifically designed to cause a severe reaction with alcohol. Alcohol must be avoided completely.

thyroxine.message: Calcium-rich foods and supplements can reduce absorption of thyroxine. Take on an empty stomach, apart from calcium.

lisinopril.message: Potassium-rich foods or salt substitutes can raise potassium to unsafe levels when combined with this medicine.

enalapril.message: Potassium-rich foods or salt substitutes can raise potassium to unsafe levels when combined with this medicine.

ramipril.message: Potassium-rich foods or salt substitutes can raise potassium to unsafe levels when combined with this medicine.

spironolactone.message: This medicine already raises potassium levels; potassium-rich foods or salt substitutes can push levels too high.

metformin.message: Heavy alcohol use with metformin increases the risk of a rare but serious condition called lactic acidosis.

theophylline.message: Caffeine can add to theophylline's stimulant effects and increase side effects like jitteriness or a rapid heartbeat.

isotretinoin.message: Vitamin A supplements combined with this medicine can cause additive toxicity. Avoid extra vitamin A supplements.

diazepam.message: Alcohol combined with this medicine can cause dangerous sedation and slowed breathing.

alprazolam.message: Alcohol combined with this medicine can cause dangerous sedation and slowed breathing.

sildenafil.message: Grapefruit juice can raise sildenafil levels in the blood, increasing the risk of side effects.

paracetamol.message: Heavy or chronic alcohol use with paracetamol increases the risk of liver damage.

ofloxacin.message: Dairy products and calcium-rich foods can reduce absorption of ofloxacin. Space apart by a couple of hours.

levofloxacin.message: Dairy products and calcium-rich foods can reduce absorption of levofloxacin. Space apart by a couple of hours.

glimepiride.message: Alcohol with glimepiride can cause severe low blood sugar and a flushing-type reaction.

itraconazole.message: Grapefruit juice can raise itraconazole levels in the blood, increasing risk of side effects.

amlodipine.message: Grapefruit juice can raise amlodipine levels, increasing risk of low blood pressure and dizziness.

clonazepam.message: Alcohol combined with this medicine can cause dangerous sedation and slowed breathing.

escitalopram oxalate.message: Alcohol can increase sedation and other side effects when combined with this medicine.

gabapentin.message: Alcohol can increase drowsiness and dizziness when combined with this medicine.

tramadol.message: Alcohol combined with tramadol increases the risk of dangerous sedation and seizures.

nortriptyline.message: Alcohol can increase sedation when combined with this medicine.

fexofenadine.message: Grapefruit, orange, or apple juice can reduce absorption of fexofenadine, making it less effective. Take with water instead.
